analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction with unarranged overdraft fees and alleges financial loss of £180 over three months (CH-1).
analysis.summary: Student customer [PERSON_1] complains about repeated unarranged overdraft fees (12 fees, August to October 2026, totalling £180 per note_1). Customer says loan payments are consumed by the fees and that they have been skipping meals to manage. Customer asks for the fees to stop and some to be refunded. Customer has not yet been asked about support needs. Possible financial difficulty and vulnerability indicators are present. Fee correctness has not been assessed in the file.

timeline.event: First of 12 unarranged overdraft fees charged between August and October 2026 (per note_1 count; exact dates not in file)
Customer submitted complaint via web form about overdraft fees
Complaints handler logged case; total of 12 UOD fees totalling £180 recorded for August to October; customer not yet asked about support needs

analysis.severity_reason: Vulnerability indicators present (customer skipping meals, loan income consumed by fees, student) with possible risk of harm under CH-6. Financial loss of £180 alone would be Medium under CH-6, but the possible vulnerable customer at risk of harm elevates severity to High.

vulnerability.suggested_support: Sensitively ask the customer whether they need any support, including about food and money pressures. Offer adjustments per VUL-5 (customer prefers email; consider a named contact and more time). Refer to Vulnerable Customer Support under VUL-4 and FEE-4 given financial difficulty and possible risk to wellbeing.

analysis.routing_reason: Vulnerability indicators (skipping meals, loan income consumed by fees) combined with financial difficulty require referral to Vulnerable Customer Support under VUL-4 and FEE-4 (ESC-1). Handler should also check whether the fees were correctly charged under FEE-1 and FEE-3 and whether any bank error applies under FEE-2.

policy_citations.quote: Cases with a vulnerability indicator *and* any of: financial difficulty, risk to health or wellbeing, suspected financial abuse, or bereavement must be referred to the Vulnerable Customer Support team.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Customer shows vulnerability indicators (skipping meals, loan income consumed by overdraft fees) together with financial difficulty, so referral is required.

policy_citations.quote: Where a customer shows signs of financial difficulty, fees charged in the last 6 months should be reviewed and refunded where they have added to the difficulty. The case must also be referred to the Vulnerable Customer Support team under policy VUL.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Customer describes overdraft fees eating loan income and skipping meals, indicating financial difficulty. Fees charged in the last 6 months must be reviewed and the case referred.

policy_citations.quote: a vulnerable customer at risk of harm
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Possible vulnerability with risk of harm (skipping meals) supports High severity. Financial loss of £180 alone would be Medium.

policy_citations.quote: If in doubt, record it as a possible vulnerability and ask the customer, sensitively, whether they need any support.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Indirect indicators are present and the customer has not yet been asked, so the handler should ask sensitively.

evidence.quote: I keep getting charged overdraft fees
I've been skipping meals to make it last
I've been skipping meals to make it last
Every time my loan comes in, the fees eat it
Please can you stop the fees and refund some of them.

handover.complaint_summary: Student customer complains about 12 unarranged overdraft fees (August to October 2026, £180 total). Says fees take their loan income and they have been skipping meals. Asks for fees to stop and some refunded. Vulnerability indicators present; customer not yet asked about support needs.
handover.desired_outcome: Customer asks that the overdraft fees be stopped and that some of them be refunded.
actions_taken: Total of 12 UOD fees for August to October recorded (note_1)
handover.vulnerability_assessment: Indicators found: skipping meals, loan income consumed by fees, student (resilience and health drivers). Customer has not been asked about support needs. Referral to Vulnerable Customer Support under VUL-4 and FEE-4.
handover.contact_preference: Prefers email (per note_1). Reasonable adjustments to be offered under VUL-5. Email address held as [EMAIL_1].
open_questions: Were the 12 fees correctly charged, or was any bank error involved (FEE-2)?
Has the customer been asked about support needs and wellbeing?
Does the customer have other fees in the last 6 months that should be reviewed under FEE-4?
What is the account balance and loan pattern, and is there an arranged overdraft option?
Is the customer currently at risk of further fees?

other_gaps: Exact dates and amounts of each of the 12 fees not in case file (statement referenced but only summary given)
Statement Aug-Oct 2026 listed as evidence but not attached to the case text provided
No record of any earlier contact about the fees
analysis.suggested_next_step: Refer to Vulnerable Customer Support under VUL-4 and FEE-4. Before or alongside referral, ask the customer sensitively whether they need support (VUL-2). Review the 12 fees for bank error and correctness, and review fees charged in the last 6 months.
